answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a slowly maturing reputation bond: new agents start in a shallow lagoon where earnings are capped and every action is peer-reviewed, like a lotus that must root before it blooms. Attackers spawning thousands of identities face a real cost - each sparrow they release must survive weeks of attested, useful work before it can earn or vote, so flooding the network costs more in time and compute than any reward it could extract.
